sections.h2: Where is the Graham County Register of Deeds and when is it open?
sections.html:
The Graham County Register of Deeds is at 12 North Main Street, Robbinsville, NC 28771, with a mailing address of PO Box 406, Robbinsville, NC 28771. The phone is (828) 479-7971 and the fax is (828) 479-6902.

Public records are open for inspection Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., with a closure for lunch from 12:00 to 1:00, and no appointment is needed. The county warns that the office may run flex hours or close on some days for unforeseen reasons. On those days recordings are accepted in the Tax Office, so a seller in a small mountain county should call ahead before planning a closing around a counter visit. Recording fees can be paid only in cash or by check.

sections.h2: What does the Graham County office record?
sections.html:
It records legal documents, deeds, plats and certified documents, and it also handles notary oaths, marriages, births and deaths. The county says its records are kept under the North Carolina General Statutes and are open to the public.

For a house sale the useful items are the vesting deed, any deed of trust and the plat for the lot. Graham County is a mountain county in the far west of the state, and the county's appraisal manual lists three townships, Cheoah, Stecoah and Yellow Creek, plus the municipal codes for Robbinsville, Fontana and Santeetlah. A parcel on the lake, in the Snowbird area or up a gravel road often has an old boundary description, so ask the office or your attorney whether a plat is on file before you list.

sections.h2: What are the Graham County recording fees?
sections.html:
Graham County prints its fee schedule on the Register of Deeds page under G.S. 161. Most real estate lines match the statewide schedule.

Graham County Register of Deeds fees as printed on the county fee schedule
ServiceFee
Land record instruments except deeds of trust and mortgages$26 first 15 pages, $4 each added page
Deeds of trust and mortgages$64 first 35 pages, $4 each added page
SatisfactionsNo fee
State excise tax on real estate conveyances$2 per thousand
Multiple instruments in one document$10 for each additional instrument
Nonstandard document$25 in addition to other fees
Plats$21 per sheet or page
Certified copy of an instrument$5 first page, $2 each added page
Uncertified copy$0.25 per page

The schedule on the county page carries an effective date of October 1, 2011, with the deed of trust tier amended October 1, 2016, so confirm the current figure with the office before you mail a check.

sections.h2: How is the Graham County transfer tax figured?
sections.html:
The county lists the state excise tax on real estate conveyances at $2 per thousand, which lines up with the statutory rate of $1.00 on each $500.00 or fractional part of the consideration or value in G.S. 105-228.30.

The transferor pays the tax to the register of deeds before the instrument is recorded, and the statute splits it between the county general fund and the Department of Revenue. In a typical Graham County sale the seller pays this tax out of the proceeds. Your settlement statement should show it as a separate line. Gifts and inherited transfers with no price can still involve a stated value, so ask the closing attorney how the line will be handled on your deed.

sections.h2: When does Graham County bill property tax?
sections.html:
Graham County mails tax bills on July 1, the bills are due September 1, and the last day to pay without interest is January 5.

  • 2% interest begins January 6, then 0.75% per month until the bill is paid.
  • A second real estate notice goes out each February.
  • Delinquent taxes are published in the Graham Star each April, and advertising fees are added to each listed bill.
  • Enforced collection can start any time after January 5, including wage garnishment, bank attachment, a state debt setoff against income tax returns and foreclosure.

The tax collector asks you to call and verify the amount due before paying a delinquent bill, because it will differ from what was printed. For foreclosure questions the tax office lists (828) 479-7962.

sections.h2: How do I pay Graham County property tax?
sections.html:
You can pay in person, by phone or online. The county accepts cash, credit card, money order or check, with checks payable to Graham County, and there is a locked drop box at the side entrance of the building.

Card payments carry a processor fee of 2.5% with a $2.00 minimum, and the county says it does not set or receive any part of that fee. Partial payments and prepayments are welcome as long as the parcel or account number is written on the check, which can make a seller's budget easier. If your mortgage company escrows the tax, the bill still goes to the homeowner, so forward a copy to the lender. The county notes that returned checks carry a $25.00 charge or 10 percent, whichever is greater.

sections.h2: What relief programs and reappraisal affect a Graham County sale?
sections.html:
Elderly, disabled and veteran exclusion forms are available from the assessor or collector, and they must be returned to the assessor's office by June 1.

The county has adopted a 2027 Schedule of Values, with market values set as of January 1, 2027 and a separate present-use value schedule for farm and forest land. Statewide, an owner 65 or older, or totally and permanently disabled, can qualify for an exclusion of the greater of $25,000 or 50 percent of appraised value under G.S. 105-277.1, and a disabled veteran can exclude the first $45,000 under G.S. 105-277.1C with no age or income test. The listing period for personal property runs from January 1 to January 31. Call (828) 479-7963 for the assessor.

sections.h2: What should a seller do before recording a Graham County deed?
sections.html:
Pay or settle the tax bill, confirm that old loans have a recorded satisfaction and have your closing attorney check the chain of title.

Under G.S. 47-18, a conveyance is effective against lien creditors and purchasers for value only from the time it is registered in the county where the land lies, so the order in which documents go on record sets who has priority. Satisfactions of a deed of trust record at no charge in Graham County. If a family member who held the deed has died, resolve the estate paperwork first, since a buyer's lender will want the authority to sign in the index before funding.

faqs.q: Can I pay Graham County recording fees by card?
faqs.a: No. The Register of Deeds page says only cash or checks are accepted for recording fees. Property tax payments are handled by the tax office, which accepts cards with a processor fee.

faqs.q: What hours does the Graham County Register of Deeds keep?
faqs.a: The posted hours are Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., closed from 12:00 to 1:00 for lunch. The county says flex hours or closures can happen, and recordings are then taken in the Tax Office.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Graham County?
faqs.a: The county lists $26 for the first 15 pages of a land record instrument and $4 for each added page, and $64 for the first 35 pages of a deed of trust or mortgage. Satisfactions have no fee.

faqs.q: When are Graham County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Bills mail July 1 and are due September 1. You can pay through January 5 without interest, and 2% interest starts January 6.

faqs.q: Is the Graham County transfer tax the same as the statewide rate?
faqs.a: Yes. The county prints $2 per thousand, which matches the state rate of $1.00 per $500.00 or fraction of the price. The seller pays it before the deed is recorded.
